text:
alex: Quick one from last week's conf in Berlin  checked bag came in overweight bc of boxes of swag we shipped back for the office. Airline charged €95 overweight fee at counter. Is that reimbursable? Also they billed an extra €12 after the trip as a "handling fee" on my card  how do I dispute that?
people-ops: Short: overweight fees for business materials are reimbursable when they are for legitimate company property (swag, samples). Please mark the expense as "equipment/shipping related" and attach proof of swag (email from events team or packing list). For post-trip extra charges, finance/card ops can help with disputes.
alex: Proof: I have the event logistics email listing items + a photo of packed boxes. Airline receipt only shows "overweight €95" and then later my bank statement shows €12 "misc charge".
finance-nina: That should be fine. Submit two expense lines: 1) €95 overweight fee (attach airline receipt + packing list), 2) €12 handling fee flagged as "disputed charge" and attach the card statement. We'll reimburse the €95 first. For the €12 we'll open a dispute with card provider; if dispute resolves in your favor we'll adjust.
alex: Do I need manager approval to claim swag shipping/overweight? It's not personal, but not a conference ticket either.
manager-asha: I approve Alex's overweight fee and confirm the items were company swag. Alex please tag the expense with project code EVENTS-Q2 and include the logistics email.
alex: Thanks Asha. For the dispute, is there anything else I should ask the airline for?
finance-nina: Ask airline for an itemized receipt or transaction reference that ties the €12 to the overweight transaction. If they say it was a "processing/authorization adjustment" get the explanation in email. Upload any correspondence; Finance will submit proof for chargeback. If the bank requires a signed dispute form we'll send you the template.
people-ops: FYI: moving swag as checked luggage is allowed but consider shipping via courier for large volumes next time; Finance can advise on cost-benefit. Also check customs rules for cross-border swag shipments as VAT/duties may apply.
alex: One more: I used my personal card because corporate card was declined at check-in. Should I file for reimbursement or card dispute?
finance-nina: Reimburse the legitimate charges on your personal card (attach receipts + manager approval). For the corporate card decline, we'll investigate with cards team; if that decline caused additional fees, mark them as "card-failure" in notes and we'll review for extra reimbursement.
cards-bot: Automated note: submit overweight receipt + packing list + event logistics email. For disputed post-trip charges, attach card statement and any airline correspondence. Reimbursements processed in original currency. Tag manager for approval for non-standard items.
alex: Perfect, uploading now. Appreciate the help :thumbsup:
